title: Article with photos and charts
purpose: Editorial article: hero photo, captioned figures from local files, inline charts from data series, pull quotes, sources.
when: A story or explainer meant to be read: newsletter piece, case study, market note, blog draft.
not_for: Internal status or KPI pages (use dashboard) and plain memos (use report-text).

schema.$defs_note: image src fields are local files (copied to <name>-files/) or URLs starting with / or http

src.description: Image file (path relative to the data file) or URL

blocks.description: The article body in order. type = text | heading | figure | gallery | chart | quote | callout

text.description: text: Markdown; heading: the heading; quote: the quote; callout: Markdown

caption.description: figure, chart: caption or source line

wide.description: figure: full column width without side margins

images.description: gallery: two or more images in a grid

columns.description: chart: label column name, then one name per series

example.title: Small solar on terraced land
example.subtitle: How hillside farms in the Peloponnese turned old olive terraces into a second harvest
example.author: Example data

hero.caption: Panels follow the old terrace lines, so the slope needs no new earthworks.

example.lead: Terraces built for olives two centuries ago now carry rows of solar panels. The trees stay; the panels sit on the flat steps between them, and the farm sells power in the hours when the grove needs nothing.

blocks.text: The idea is simple. A terrace is already level, already drained and already reachable by a path. Mounting frames need little more than a few ground screws, and the panels shade the soil just enough to keep it from drying out in August.
Output follows the season, with a long plateau from May to August. The figures below are illustrative and labelled as example data.

blocks.text: We used to harvest once a year. Now the hill pays us every month.
